sources.entry: Liftoff - Open-source Launchpad replacement with live window previews, window-title search, and one-click folder organizing. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/firstfu/Liftoff) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Liftoff is an open-source, macOS 26+ Launchpad replacement with live window thumbnails, window-title search, and a built-in table for one-click Smart Organize of apps into folders.
summary.what_it_does: Liftoff restores the classic Launchpad grid (pages, folders, drag to rearrange, type to search) for macOS 26, which replaced it with an "Apps" list. Resting the pointer on a running app, or pressing Space on it, shows thumbnails of its windows, including minimized windows and windows on other desktops, and clicking one switches to it. Search matches app names, initials (e.g. "vsc" for Visual Studio Code), pinyin for Chinese names, and open window titles. Smart Organize sorts apps into folders using a built-in table of 1,000+ apps, with a preview before anything is applied and an automatic layout backup. Other features include dragging apps to the Dock, importing an old Launchpad layout, several ways to open the panel (hotkey, trackpad pinch, hot corner, Dock icon, or a liftoff:// URL), wallpaper and appearance options, multi-display support, and 13 interface languages.
use_cases: replace the Launchpad grid on macOS 26
find and switch to open windows quickly
organize a cluttered Mac app collection into folders
preview window thumbnails of running apps
drag apps from the launcher to the Dock
uninstall Mac apps along with leftover files
back up and restore Launchpad layout
how_to_run: Download Liftoff.zip from the GitHub releases page and move Liftoff.app to /Applications
xcodebuild -project Liftoff.xcodeproj -scheme Liftoff -configuration Release -derivedDataPath build build
notable: Smart Organize uses a built-in lookup table of 1,000+ apps with no AI and no network, so results are deterministic and previewed before applying
Live window thumbnails of a running app's windows, with click-to-jump including minimized windows
Search matches window titles as well as app names, initials, and pinyin
Published performance claims (panel opens in under 3 ms, 0% CPU when idle) with a scripts/selftest.sh to reproduce them
Releases signed with a consistent certificate so macOS keeps Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions across updates
caveats: Not yet notarized by Apple, so the first launch needs a manual Open Anyway step in System Settings
Needs Screen & System Audio Recording permission for window previews and optionally Accessibility
